bib.title: Logic-of-Thought: Injecting Logic into Contexts for Full Reasoning in Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Logic-of-Thought: Injecting Logic into Contexts for Full Reasoning in Large Language Models", Tongxuan Liu, Wenjiang Xu, Weizhe Huang, Yuting Zeng, Jiaxing Wang, Xingyu Wang, Hailong Yang, Jing Li. arXiv 2409.17539v2 (cs.CL), 7 Feb 2025. The footer reads like a venue-less arXiv version, so treat it as a preprint. The file is named 2024. Code: github.com/HEA1OR/lot.

COVERAGE: 68,064 of 68,064 chars read, which covers all 18 pages. That includes the body, limitations, appendices A-E (case studies, error analysis tables 6-8, prompts) and the reference list. I skimmed the rest of the prompts in E.3 and E.4 (SatLM and ToT prompt templates), which are long templates. Figure 3 (SatLM comparison bar chart) extracted as garbled glyphs, so its values are unread. Figure 5's values did extract.

CLAIMS
1. LoT is a zero-shot prompt augmentation, not a solver.
- claim: An LLM extracts propositions and implications. A Python program expands them with logic laws. An LLM translates the results back to English, which is appended to the full original context. The original text is kept, which is how it avoids the information loss of LINC and SatLM.
  number: none
  setup: three phases (Logic Extraction, Logic Extension, Logic Translation). Connectives are only ¬, → and ∧. Laws are only Double Negation, Contraposition and Transitive.
  quote: "LoT first extracts propositions and logical expressions from the input context, expands these logical expressions according to logical reasoning laws, and converts the deduced logical expressions back into natural language form. Then LoT considers these extended logical descriptions as additional logical augmentation for LLMs and concatenates it with the original context"
  where: p.2 (Intro)
2. Main result: LoT adds to nearly every baseline.
- claim: LoT improved the baseline in 37 of 40 comparisons, and LoT+CoT-SC(5) was best on all five datasets with GPT-3.5.
  number: 37/40
  setup: GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 and GPT-4-0613, zero-shot, default sampling parameters. Baselines Direct, CoT, SC(5), CoT-SC(5). Datasets ReClor (46 items, implication subset only), LogiQA (1302), RuleTaker (967, closed-world, depth 5), ProofWriter (985, closed-world, depth 5), FOLIO (135, closed-world).
  quote: "Among total 40 comparisons (including four baseline prompting methods across five datasets with two LLMs), LoT significantly enhances the performance of baseline prompting methods in 37 instances."
  where: Sec 4.4, p.5
3. Headline gains and Table 1 examples.
- claim: Abstract gains are +4.35 (CoT, ReClor), +3.52 (CoT-SC, RuleTaker) and +8 (ToT, ProofWriter). Table 1 examples with GPT-3.5: Direct on ReClor 46.20 to LoT 56.02. Direct on FOLIO 68.89 to LoT 76.00. CoT on ReClor 52.17 to LoT+CoT 56.52. GPT-4 gains are much smaller.
  number: ReClor Direct 46.20 -> 56.02; FOLIO 68.89 -> 76.00; GPT-4 Direct FOLIO 82.96 -> 83.55; GPT-4 Direct LogiQA 59.22 -> 60.11
  setup: as claim 2. ReClor n=46, so +4.35 is 2 questions.
  quote: "Direct 46.20 36.44 51.89 52.87 68.89 72.17 59.22 64.30 63.74 82.96 / LoT 56.02 ↑9.82 36.85 ↑0.41 59.44 ↑7.55 59.35 ↑6.48 76.00 ↑7.11 77.98 ↑5.81 60.11 ↑0.89 64.65 ↑0.35 65.58 ↑1.84 83.55 ↑0.59"
  where: Table 1, p.4
4. LoT alone matches or beats CoT in most cells.
- claim: LoT alone beats CoT in 8 of 10 dataset/model pairs.
  number: 8/10
  setup: as claim 2. In Table 1, GPT-3.5 CoT beats LoT on LogiQA (39.75 vs 36.85) and FOLIO (81.19 vs 76.00).
  quote: "LoT achieves significant enhancements in the accuracy of Direct across all datasets and outperforms CoT in eight out of ten sets of comparative data."
  where: Sec 4.4, p.5. My check of Table 1 does not obviously give 8 of 10. For GPT-3.5, LoT is below CoT on 4 of 5 (LogiQA, RuleTaker 59.44 vs 60.56, ProofWriter 59.35 vs 61.02, FOLIO), and above only on ReClor. Treat the claim as unverified from the table.
5. Regressions exist.
- claim: LoT hurt GPT-4 on LogiQA, and sometimes hurt GPT-3.5 on FOLIO. The authors blame extraction errors.
  number: -0.57 (GPT-4 LogiQA, CoT), -1.38 (GPT-4 LogiQA, CoT-SC), -2.23 (GPT-3.5 FOLIO, CoT)
  setup: Table 1.
  quote: "LoT+CoT and LoT+CoT-SC marginally trailed behind CoT and CoT-SC, recording a decline of 0.57% and 1.38% respectively."
  where: Sec 4.4, p.5
6. LoT beats the neuro-symbolic methods LINC and SatLM, which underperform plain Direct.
- claim: On FOLIO, LINC scores far below Direct. LoT is higher than both.
  number: LINC 45.19 / 55.56 vs LoT 76.00 / 83.55
  setup: LINC rerun with its public code and original settings (8-shot). LoT is zero-shot. GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 and GPT-4-0613. The SatLM comparison used GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct, one-shot, on the 46 ReClor items. Values are in Fig 3, which is unreadable.
  quote: "Direct 68.89 82.96 / LINC 45.19 55.56 / LoT 76.00 83.55"
  where: Table 2, p.5. The SatLM gains over Direct, CoT and SC (+1.74, +2.18, +6.52) are in the text, but they are LoT's gains over those baselines, not over SatLM.
  Caveat: the LINC comparison is few-shot against zero-shot, with a different setup.
7. ToT.
- claim: LoT lifts ToT by 8 points on ProofWriter depth 5. Direct is near chance.
  number: Direct 51, ToT 70, LoT+ToT 78
  setup: GPT-4-0613, few-shot, 100 random depth-5 ProofWriter validation items. ToT reimplemented from Yifan et al. 2024 (Cumulative Reasoning).
  quote: "Direct only achieves performance similar to random guessing (50%). The accuracy rate of ToT is +19% higher than Direct, reaching 70%"
  where: Sec 4.6 and Fig 5, p.6. The text says "+8% increase in accuracy compared to ToT". Fig 5 values 51/70/78/50 are mixed, with a stray "50" for the chance line. n=100.
  Mechanism (Table 3): ToT total states 18.70 vs LoT+ToT 19.10, successful states 7.70 vs 8.09, full reasoning 90% vs 92%.
8. Ablations.
- claim: Dropping the Contraposition Law, or keeping only half the generated descriptions, lowers FOLIO accuracy. Skipping the Extension step (translating extracted expressions without deduction) barely changes results.
  number: FOLIO 76.00 -> 72.22 (no contraposition) / 72.96 (half of descriptions). Extension ablation: LogiQA 36.85 -> 36.79, RuleTaker 59.44 -> 59.05
  setup: GPT-4-0613, FOLIO, for Table 4. Table 5 is GPT-3.5, since 36.85 and 59.44 match the GPT-3.5 LoT row.
  quote: "LoT 76.00 / w/o Contraposition Law 72.22 / w/o Half of Generated Description 72.96"
  where: Table 4, p.6. There is a discrepancy: Table 4's 76.00 is the GPT-3.5 value in Table 1, yet the text says GPT-4-0613. GPT-4 LoT on FOLIO is 83.55. Flag this. Table 5: "LoT w/o Extension 36.79 59.05" vs Direct 36.44 and 51.89. The extension adds almost nothing on LogiQA and about 0.4 on RuleTaker. Most of the gain comes from the extraction and restatement step.
9. Error analysis: extraction is the weak point.
- claim: With GPT-3.5 on FOLIO, 40% of samples had a wrong extraction. LoT was net positive anyway (18.52% fixed vs 11.85% broken).
  number: 40% extraction errors, 5.18% translation errors, 0% extension errors, 42.22% at least one error
  setup: GPT-3.5-turbo-0125, FOLIO, 135 items, Direct vs LoT.
  quote: "it was observed that 40% of the samples encountered errors during the logical extraction phase. No errors were recorded during logical expansion. Additionally, 5.18% of the samples experienced errors in the logical translation stage."
  where: App D, Tables 6-8
  Also: with wrong extraction, 10.37% went wrong to right and 6.67% went right to wrong. Errors do not always hurt, because the final LLM reads natural language and the original context. Fig 4 case: a wrong A→B gave a wrong A→C, but the LLM corrected it on translation.
10. CoT and LoT overlap.
- claim: On simple chains, both CoT and LoT just chain conditionals.
  number: none
  quote: "CoT and LoT sometimes have overlapping capabilities."
  where: App C.

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Sec 7): only three connectives and three laws, with more being harder to prompt and deduce. LLM hallucination in extraction (repeated expressions, omitted relations, deviating propositions) still causes failures.
- Small and cherry-picked subsets: ReClor is only 46 items (implication questions only), FOLIO 135 (CWA only), ToT study 100. Only depth-5 closed-world for ProofWriter and RuleTaker. No significance tests or variance. Single run, with unspecified temperature.
- Only GPT-3.5 and GPT-4-0613 (non-reasoning, old models). No reasoning models. Gains shrink on GPT-4 (often under 2 points). These models are dated by now.
- Baselines for neuro-symbolic comparisons use different shot counts and models (LINC 8-shot, SatLM one-shot on GPT-3.5-instruct). The Logic-LM comparison was not run.
- Extra LLM calls are needed (extraction plus translation). Cost and latency are not reported.
- The "37 of 40" claim counts any increase as "significant". Table 1 shows several zeros or small gains.
- Extension ablation shows the deduction step adds little on LogiQA and RuleTaker.

BUILDS ON
- CoT: Kojima et al. 2022, Wei et al. 2022, Nye et al. 2021.
- Self-Consistency: Wang et al. 2022b.
- ToT: Yao et al. 2024, with the reimplementation from Yifan et al. 2024 (Cumulative Reasoning).
- Context extension by logic laws: LReasoner (Wang et al. 2022a).
- Neuro-symbolic: Faithful CoT (Lyu et al. 2023), LINC (Olausson et al. 2023), Logic-LM (Pan et al. 2023), SatLM (Ye et al. 2024).
- Unfaithful CoT: Bao et al. 2024, Lanham et al. 2023, Lyu et al. 2023, Turpin et al. 2024.
- Logic background: Büning and Lettmann 1999.
- Datasets: ReClor, LogiQA, RuleTaker, ProofWriter, FOLIO.

CODE
No code in the paper body. The Logic Extension step is described as a Python implementation of transitive and contraposition rules, but the program is not printed. Prompts are in Appendix E.
- Extraction prompt (App E.1, ReClor/LogiQA): "Please use uppercase English letters such as A , B , C , etc . to identify all possible propositions . Do not include negative tones such as "not" in the propositions ... A causal expression is only established when the context directly supports this relationship . Use arrows (→) to indicate causal relationships ... Finally , output propositions and causal expressions ."
- Translation prompt (E.2): "Please use the provided propositions to translate each expression into a complete sentence ... Only output the sentences in a paragraph !"

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): LINC vs LoT on the Harry/Walden example. LINC drops Person(Harry) and Book(Walden), so Prover9 answers "Uncertain". LoT adds "If a person reads a book, that person become smarter". The clearest picture of the information-loss argument.
- Fig 2 (p.3): three-phase pipeline on the keyboarding example, ¬A→¬B and ¬B→¬C giving C→A.
- Fig 4 (p.5): SatLM vs LoT case on ReClor (great apes).
- Fig 5 (p.6): ToT vs LoT+ToT bars.
- Fig 6 (App A): state exploration with and without LoT.
- Fig 7 (App B): extraction error case.
I did not run the figures script.

PROBLEMS
- Fig 3 text is garbled, so SatLM numbers are unreadable. Tables 1-2 extracted cleanly. The negation symbol is lost in some extracted prompt text ("A" instead of ¬A).
- Discrepancy: Table 4 text says GPT-4, but 76.00 is the GPT-3.5 FOLIO LoT number.
- Claim 4 (8 of 10) does not obviously match Table 1.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
